summary: dbmcp Docker/config/code-layout details from dbmcp/README.md (delta over proposals 01-02).

ops.text: The dbmcp folder is a standalone Docker package for the KitchenHQ SQLite MCP server.
ops.quote: This folder is a standalone Docker package for the KitchenHQ SQLite MCP server

ops.text: The dbmcp MCP endpoint is available at `http://localhost:18000/mcp`.
ops.quote: The MCP endpoint is available at `http://localhost:18000/mcp`

ops.text: dbmcp can be built and run standalone with `docker build -t kitchenhq-db-mcp .` and `docker run --rm -p 18000:18000 -e KITCHENHQ_API_KEY=your-key -v "${PWD}/data:/data" kitchenhq-db-mcp`.
The SQLite database is stored in the host `data` folder mounted at `/data`; the container always accesses it as `/data/kitchen.db` and only the host-side location changes.
ops.quote: The container always accesses the database as `/data/kitchen.db`; only the host-side location changes

ops.text: The dbmcp container always serves over streamable HTTP.
ops.quote: The container always serves over streamable HTTP

ops.text: `KITCHENHQ_API_KEY` (required), `KITCHEN_DB_PATH`, `MCP_HOST` and `MCP_PORT` can be overridden with environment variables.
ops.quote: `KITCHEN_DB_PATH`, `MCP_HOST`, and `MCP_PORT` can be overridden with environment variables

ops.text: The `kitchendb/` package consists of `config`, `db`, `schema`, `seed`, `validation` and `models` modules, `tools/` (data operations by domain, each an MCP tool and/or a REST handler), `routes.py`, and `server.py` (`create_app()`).
The compatibility shim `init_db.py` also supports `from init_db import DATABASE_PATH`.

The inventory-mutation REST routes (`POST /api/inventory`, `PATCH /api/inventory/{id}`, `POST /api/inventory/{id}/discard`) are kept because pytest exercises them and they mirror live MCP tools, even though the read-only chatui Pantry page no longer calls them.
ops.quote: pytest exercises them and they mirror live

ops.text: An example daily backup schedule is the cron entry `0 3 * * * KITCHEN_DB_PATH=/path/to/kitchen.db python /path/to/dbmcp/scripts/backup_db.py` (or Windows Task Scheduler).
